claim: The piezo controller reports each of its three channels' calibrated position range as 0 to 600 um (0 to 6.0e8 picometres, as reported).

numbers.name: piezo_calibrated_range_min
numbers.note: the same on channels 1, 2 and 3; reported as -0.000000000e+000 pm

numbers.name: piezo_calibrated_range_max
numbers.note: the same on channels 1, 2 and 3; reported as 6.000000000e+008 pm

validity_conditions: A device's report of itself, read in a preparatory run -- a read-only first contact that sent only .get commands from a list the person approved by sha256, and moved nothing. 11-21 condition 4 as narrowed at 20a688b lets such a report enter citing the run, graded as an observation by this system; it is not a measurement of any registered observable, and check 85 counts it rather than failing it. E1 from `measured:`. THIS IS NOT A LIMIT. What software may command is the person's, in envelope/safety.json, and the store holds none of it; that the person's software range happens also to be 0 to 600 um is a coincidence of numbers, not a shared source. It DISAGREES with the person's statement that the device range is -100 to 600 um (piezo_device_range_as_stated_by_the_person), and the two are kept side by side, not reconciled (rule 7): a calibrated range and a mechanical range are not obviously the same quantity, and which one a question needs is the caller's to say. The picometre values are converted to um exactly; nothing is estimated. Slot: A7 (what positions are within calibration).
